title: Your boss thinks you worked all weekend on this deck
experiment: none: a bet slot and a sequel to the #06 hit (the same promise, a reward in front of someone who matters, with a new tool). First English reel, so the first try of channel test T3; also a series reel for T2 (its own English numbering).
look: illustrated story (brand/story.js, brand/scenes.js), my face and body in the shirt outfit, Priya Ma'am as the boss, Rohan sends the link, compact captions
sendTo: the friend who still makes slides by hand
style: Natural, friendly American English, like a friend who tells you a short story and lets you in on a useful find. Confident, clear and brisk, one even tone for the whole story, with only a short breath between sentences. No acting, no exaggeration.

claims: Gamma has a free plan: the pricing page, plan 'Free', 'No credit card required'.
Ten slides from one prompt: 'Create up to 10 slides per prompt' (Free).
Design and pictures: 'Simple presentations ... and images' (Free); 'The best image models, built in' (home).
Export to a real PowerPoint file is free: 'Export to PDF, PPTX, PNG & Google Slides' under 'Free includes'.
Story, not data: 'about a minute' and 'one minute' (an unverified story claim, allowed by the Claims rules).
Not claimed: any price, unlimited use (credits run out), or no Gamma branding on the free plan.

sentences: Your boss thinks you worked all weekend on this deck.
It is Sunday night, and the deck is due at nine tomorrow.
All you have is one empty slide.
Then Rohan sends you a link to Gamma.
Ten slides, with a design and pictures, in about a minute.
But here is the best part.
Click Export, and it is a real PowerPoint file.
On Monday, your boss asks how long it took.
Want the link to this tool?
Send this to the friend who still makes slides by hand.
